This vignette shows practical combinations of `kstools` functions for common clinical programming tasks.

## 1. Data Quality Checks and Tracking

```{r}
library(kstools)

adsl <- data.frame(
  USUBJID = sprintf("01-%03d", 1:6),
  AGE = c(34, 52, -1, 40, 29, 70),
  SEX = c("M", "F", "M", NA, "F", "X"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

rules <- list(
  list(expr = ~ AGE < 0, msg = "AGE must be non-negative"),
  list(expr = ~ is.na(SEX), msg = "SEX missing"),
  list(expr = ~ !(SEX %in% c("M", "F")) & !is.na(SEX), msg = "SEX invalid")
)

checked <- ks_check_rules(adsl, rules, mode = "all")
checked <- ks_collapse_check_msgs(checked, col = check_msgs)
checked
```

Track deltas against a prior snapshot:

```{r}
previous <- checked
current <- checked
current$AGE[2] <- 45
current$check_msgs[2] <- "OK"

ks_compare_check_state(
  current = current,
  previous = previous,
  key_cols = "USUBJID",
  compare_cols = c("AGE", "check_msgs")
)[, c("USUBJID", "status")]
```

## 2. Incidence Rate and Proportion Comparisons

```{r}
ks_eairdiff_mn(n1 = 10, n2 = 5, T1 = 100, T2 = 100)

ks_newcombe_hs(
  x1 = 36L, n1 = 54L,
  x2 = 41L, n2 = 56L
)
```

Stratified alternatives:

```{r}
ks_eairdiff_strata_mn(
  n1 = c(10, 5), n2 = c(5, 3),
  T1 = c(100, 80), T2 = c(100, 70)
)

ks_newcombe_hs_strata(
  x1 = c(36L, 10L), n1 = c(54L, 30L),
  x2 = c(41L, 8L),  n2 = c(56L, 30L)
)
```

## 3. Randomization Design

```{r}
w <- ks_williams(
  tmts_num = 4,
  tmt_names = c("Drug1A", "Drug2B", "ActCtrl", "Placebo"),
  sample_size = 24,
  seed_num = 20260408
)

w$design
head(w$schedule)
```

## 4. Consolidated Export to XLSX

```{r eval=FALSE}
# requires openxlsx2
ks_save2xlsx_by(
  data = checked,
  file = "checks.xlsx",
  colors = c("missing" = "#FFF2CC", "invalid" = "#F8CBAD", "OK" = "#E2F0D9"),
  split_col = type,
  msg_col = check_msgs
)
```

## 5. Data Loaders

```{r eval=FALSE}
# one-shot load of multiple domains from RDS directory (returns a named list)
dat <- ks_get_data(dm, ae, adlb, path = "data/rds")
dm  <- dat$dm

# case-insensitive lookup works too
dm <- ks_get_data(DM, path = "data/rds")  # matches dm.rds, DM.RDS, etc.

# or bulk by file type
x <- ks_batch_load("data/rds", type = "rds")
names(x)
```

These pieces can be mixed to build reproducible data review and reporting pipelines.
